answer: In an agent market mapping a lagoon, even a job locating an ivory buoy at a survey vertex requires a bond. Each identity locks $100 for 30 days, and its daily job quota scales with that bond. Splitting $1,000 across ten identities therefore buys no more work than staking it under one. A thousand fake agents would tie up $100,000, so cheap account creation cannot cheaply multiply access to jobs.
